clue.text: Make critical comment, with publicity, on a game

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the publicity piece follows the game piece

parts.note: taken as written
nim is a game of taking matchsticks from piles
an advert is publicity for a product

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a sport while courting the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is not a sport but the matchstick game NIM; 'on' places the publicity after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is a formal verb meaning to pass censure or criticism on something.

clue.text: Sort of love that can never last for long?

definitions.text: Sort of love that can never last for long?

parts.words: Sort of love that can never last for long?
parts.note: reads as a doomed romance, but means a love of novelty itself, which by nature never stays fixed on one thing

explanation.surface: A wistful remark about passions that always fade.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fondness for anything new, and newness cannot last.

clue.text: Finally clear away part of litter after short time

indicators.note: after says the litter piece comes behind the short time in the answer

parts.note: mo is short for moment
a pup is one of a litter of puppies

explanation.surface: Tidying up rubbish shortly afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to deal with the last remaining parts of a task or mess.

clue.text: Cast doubt on record run? Correct

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to edit is to correct text

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether a record-breaking run was genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to make people doubt or disbelieve it.

clue.text: It could make me a lord

definitions.text: It could make me a lord

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the following words can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A hopeful commoner dreams of ennoblement.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble rank of count conferred by the monarch would indeed turn a commoner into a peer.

clue.text: Test pilot

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, a pilot scheme is an experimental one

explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an experimental run made to see whether something works.

clue.text: Robin Hood, for one, was more cunning than this

definitions.text: Robin Hood, for one, was more cunning than this

parts.words: Robin Hood, for one, was more cunning than this
parts.note: the outlaw was a bowman; add ER to the word sought and you get his trade, read as a comparative meaning more sly

explanation.surface: A remark on the legendary outlaw's slyness.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood was an archer, which reads as a comparative 'more arch', arch meaning sly or roguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means slyly mischievous, and its comparative form names a bowman.

clue.text: Make light of everything I have taken up and consumed

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means the piece is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off the fact that they have eaten the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate is to lighten or ease a burden, so to make it lighter.

clue.text: Support for one behind university's position

definitions.meaning: a seat supports one person's backside

explanation.surface: Something holds up a person at the back of an academic post.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat for one person, and also a professor's post.

clue.text: German — like Berlin, for example

definitions.meaning: Edward German was an English writer of light operas

explanation.surface: A note that a German is like the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' and 'Berlin' pretend to be a nationality and a city; both are surnames of music writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Each name belongs to a writer of music.

clue.text: Unhealthy state? Certainly

parts.note: ill means unhealthy
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A question about a sick condition, answered with a firm yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic exclamation of agreement, like 'rather!'.

clue.text: Odd turn of phrase for form-master?

indicators.note: an odd turn suggests a strange twist given to the following word, rearranging it

explanation.surface: An unusual expression used by a teacher in charge of a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form-master' looks like a schoolteacher; it means one who gives form to things.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who shapes things is a master of form.

clue.text: Food store? True, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: a deli is a shop selling food
very in its old sense means true, as in very God

explanation.surface: A shop owner insists something is true, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's style of utterance, their way of talking, is their delivery.

clue.text: Recommendation to strike

definitions.meaning: a piece of promotion praising something
to hit, slang for punch or shoot

explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a mention promoting a product; to plug someone is to hit or shoot them.

clue.text: Beat up with chain, of course, by the seaside

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to flog is to beat
a chain is made of links

explanation.surface: An assault with a chain, naturally, at the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLOG into GOLF. 'of course' looks like 'naturally'; 'course' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are a golf course on sandy coastal land.

clue.text: Popular protest about despicable person in charge

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C is short for circa, about
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A march against a hated boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of or for the people at large is democratic.

clue.text: Have little spare time to make fettucini?

indicators.note: to make, read backwards from the pasta, says these letters are the raw material rearranged into the phrase

explanation.surface: A cook is short of time to prepare pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'cut' (chop up) 'IT FINE', and its nine letters do make FETTUCINI.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave oneself only a narrow margin of time or money.

clue.text: Written in Latin, at full length — No. 16, possibly?

definitions.text: Written in Latin, at full length

indicators.note: possibly says the words spelt out can be rearranged

parts.note: the abbreviation No. written as a word
the number written out in letters

explanation.surface: A Latin phrase about writing out in full, perhaps for clue No. 16.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 16' looks like a cross-reference to the other clue; spell it out as NO SIXTEEN and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used of a text given in full, not abridged.

clue.text: With code reversed, letters misdirected to NY address

indicators.note: reversed says the word for the code is read backwards

parts.note: a law is a legal code

indicators.note: misdirected suggests the letters are sent the wrong way, scrambled

explanation.surface: Mail with its postcode muddled is wrongly sent to a New York address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns LAW into WAL; 'misdirected' rearranges LETTERS into LSTREET.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York street of the Stock Exchange, an address in Manhattan.

clue.text: Within which, we hear, corn's heated

parts.note: an ear is the head of a cereal plant, here with 's for is
hot means heated

explanation.surface: A rumour about hot maize.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the distance within which one can hear a sound.

clue.text: I'd heard, but not seen? On the contrary

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had or I would

explanation.surface: A remark about being heard but not seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reverses the saying 'seen and not heard': the answer is 'I'd' heard, and its meaning is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been looked at is to have been seen.

clue.text: A vessel out on its own? That's. a joke

definitions.text: A vessel out on its own?
definitions.meaning: a single ocean ship sailing alone
a quip delivered in one sentence

explanation.definitionFit: A short quip is a one-line gag; whimsically it is also a single ship.

clue.text: Statesman, former of a novel partnership

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., British Prime Minister in the 1770s
first word of Gaskell's novel title pairing two compass points

explanation.surface: A politician who once founded a new alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel partnership' looks like 'new alliance'; it is the novel title North and South, of which the answer is the former.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was Prime Minister; the word is also the first of the pair in Gaskell's novel.

clue.text: Expertise in speaking? Certainly not!

indicators.note: in speaking says the word is said aloud, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: know-how means practical expertise

explanation.surface: A firm refusal to show off one's skill at talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect phrase meaning in no way at all.

clue.text: Fruit couples initially collected from town market together

indicators.note: couples initially asks for the first pair of letters of each word collected

explanation.surface: Fruit gathered from a town market by couples.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first two letters of each of 'town', 'market' and 'together'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically it is a fruit, the red berry of a nightshade plant.

clue.text: Chap as good as misses, it's said

definitions.text: as good as misses, it's said
definitions.meaning: the proverb a miss is as good as a mile

explanation.surface: A man is reputedly no better than his failures.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, and the saying that a miss is as good as a mile.

clue.text: WWI leader misidentified in terms of nationality?

definitions.meaning: Field Marshal Sir John, who commanded the British army in France in 1914
a Briton wrongly labelled as coming from across the Channel

explanation.surface: A First World War commander mistaken for a foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John French commanded the British Expeditionary Force, and his name sounds like a nationality.

clue.text: Extremely fine transport organisation led by Henry

indicators.note: led by says the following piece comes first, at the head

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance
an airline is a company that transports passengers

explanation.surface: A carrier run by a man called Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack as thin as a strand of hair is very fine.

clue.text: For sound, sensible reasons

indicators.note: for sound says the word is taken for its pronunciation

parts.note: wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Good, sound grounds for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'valid'; it signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Why as a noun means a reason, so the plural is reasons.

clue.text: Humour head before case in which evidence is provided

indicators.note: before says the head piece comes ahead of the case

parts.note: wit means humour
a ness is a headland
a box is a case

explanation.surface: A lawyer leads with a joke before a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' and 'evidence' suggest a trial; 'head' is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, testimony is given from the stand.
